Extract the components of a gcTMB fit

Source: R/extract.R
gcTMB-extract.Rd

gcTMB has its own generics fixef, ranef and VarCorr and does not need nlme or lme4. They have the same names as the generics of nlme (re-exported by lme4), and work together with them: whichever package is attached last, fixef, ranef and VarCorr work both for gcTMB fits and for the fits of nlme and lme4 (the gcTMB generics pass other objects on to nlme, if it is installed). The results for gcTMB fits have the format of lme4: ranef a list of data frames, one for each term, also for a single term (nlme returns a data frame for a single level of grouping), and VarCorr a list of covariance matrices (nlme returns a character table).

Usage

fixef(object, ...)

ranef(object, ...)

VarCorr(x, sigma = 1, ...)

# Default S3 method
fixef(object, ...)

# Default S3 method
ranef(object, ...)

# Default S3 method
VarCorr(x, sigma = 1, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gcTMB'
fixef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gcTMB'
ranef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gcTMB'
VarCorr(x, sigma = 1, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gcTMB'
sigma(object, ...)

corpars(object)

varpars(object)

Arguments

object, x

A gcTMB object, the result of gcTMB.

...

Not used.

x, object

For the generics, a fitted model of any class.

sigma

Not used; for compatibility with the generic of nlme.

Value

fixef returns the coefficients of the parameters b1-b5, named as in coef: the estimated coefficients and the coefficients fixed by the user (e.g. an asymmetry b5 fixed at a value other than 1), without the variance parameters and without the defaults b4 = 0 and b5 = 1.

ranef returns a list with a data frame for each random effect term, named by its grouping factor: a row for each level and a column for each random coefficient (e.g. b1, or b1:x for a random slope of b1 in x). The random effects are the conditional modes, on the scale of the linear predictors of the parameters (the scale of the link).

VarCorr returns a list with the covariance matrix of the random effects of each term, named as in ranef, with the standard deviations and the correlation matrix as attributes stddev and correlation; the residual standard deviation is the attribute sc.

sigma returns the residual standard deviation of a gaussian model (of log(y) for lognormal; the maximum likelihood estimate, while nlme::gnls reports it with n - p degrees of freedom), or the dispersion parameter of the other families as printed by print.gcTMB (precision, size or dispersion), and NA for poisson and binomial models. The residual variance is sigma(object)^2. For gaussian models without random effects and small-sample inference (see gcTMB), it is the unbiased estimate.

corpars returns the parameter of the autocorrelation of the residuals within groups (see corStruct), rho, the correlation of residuals one unit of time apart, and an empty vector for a model with independent residuals; it is coef(fit$modelStruct$corStruct, unconstrained=FALSE) of nlme. varpars returns the parameters of the variance function of the residuals, as a named vector; the current models have a constant residual variance, so it returns an empty vector, as the extractor for a variance function once it is added.

Details

Extractors for the estimated parts of a model: the fixed effects, the predicted random effects, the covariance matrices of the random effects, the residual standard deviation, and the parameters of the residual autocorrelation and of the variance function.

Examples

fit <- gcTMB(height ~ DAS, rform=b1 + b2 ~ 1 | plant_ID, data=FabaHeights25)
fixef(fit)
#> b1:(Intercept) b2:(Intercept) b3:(Intercept) 
#>      121.08844       30.86626       12.84146 
head(ranef(fit)$plant_ID)
#>             b1         b2
#> 6    9.7005206  0.9458512
#> 7    0.3047415  1.5134969
#> 8  -10.0012561 -0.8431203
#> 9    9.4344827  2.9126002
#> 10   3.5648711 -0.9288945
#> 11   1.8398292  2.0643038
VarCorr(fit)
#> $plant_ID
#>            b1        b2
#> b1 104.794030 -3.159913
#> b2  -3.159913  6.558684
#> attr(,"stddev")
#>        b1        b2 
#> 10.236896  2.560993 
#> attr(,"correlation")
#>            b1         b2
#> b1  1.0000000 -0.1205309
#> b2 -0.1205309  1.0000000
#> 
#> attr(,"sc")
#> [1] 2.074042
sigma(fit)^2
#> [1] 4.301651
corpars(fit)
#> named numeric(0)
varpars(fit)
#> named numeric(0)
